Which shot, which effect

Every effect in our library, re-rendered on the clip it suits best from the Content Hub and Drive, and scored. Use the shoot list to plan tomorrow: pick the effects, then shoot the matching setup.

Re-scored 14 Nov against the original reels. The earlier 9s judged how clean each sample looked, not how close it is to the reel it copies. Every effect has now been compared frame by frame with its original and scored on match, looks, technical quality and overall. Overall can be at most one point above match. Nothing reaches 9 yet; each card says what to change.

Fix progress. Every version is kept: each card plays its best-scoring version and lists all of them (v01, v02 …) with their scores, so you can compare or go back. 70–86: all 16 now score 9 against the original (84 vertigo still needs new footage). 01–14 and 31–63 rebuilt once: about 5 → 7.7. 15–29 rebuilt up to five times: 15, 16 and 20 score 9, the rest 8.3–8.8. Scores are from independent reviewers.

Art-director audit, 24 Nov. Every effect with an original in Vibha's grid was put side by side with ours and graded by eye: font, richness, cleanness, layout. The graphics are mostly close; the shots are not. Vibha films every effect in one warm, lamp-lit, wide room with soft focus; ours sit on busy murals, harsh office light or tight close-ups. Nothing is a true 9 side by side: best is 8.5 (12, 15, 22, 31, 44, 52, 61). The gold pill on each card is this audit; the number in the corner is the older reviewer score. One shoot fixes most of the gap: see "Vibha-style plate" in the shoot list.

Shoot for Hiral

These 7 effects cannot match the original from the footage we have. Each needs a short new clip of Hiral. Hand this list to whoever is filming. The blue cards below repeat each brief next to the effect.

Phone on a tripod, filmed from behind

87 glass-slam · 88 hand-from-screen · 89 zoom-wheel

One set covers three effects. Shoot all three in one session.

87 glass-slam: Two cameras. Camera A (Canon, the hero shot): vertical, on a tripod, ~60 cm behind a phone that is itself on a small tripod; frame so the phone fills ~70% of the height with the room visible around it, focus on the phone screen. The phone (camera B): iPhone in video mode, rear camera facing Hiral, screen facing camera A, brightness at max, Do Not Disturb on. Set: a homely room (bed, sofa or plants), warm light, phone ~1.2 m off the floor. Action: Hiral starts 3-4 m back from the phone, centred. On 'action' she walks briskly toward it (2 s), then leans in and presses both open palms and her face (cheek or nose) flat onto the phone screen, holds 1 s, smiles, pulls back. She can laugh. Total ~5 s. Line, optional, as she pulls back: 'Okay, now I have your attention.' Takes: 5, including one with only palms (no face) as a safe option. Clean the phone glass between takes. Avoid knocking the phone tripod (weigh it down), ceiling lights reflecting on the screen, and walking off-centre.

88 hand-from-screen: Same set as glass slam: Canon vertical on a tripod behind and slightly above a phone on a small tripod, phone filling ~70% of frame height, warm homely room, phone screen at max brightness showing its camera view of Hiral. Hiral sits cross-legged or on a chair ~1 m in front of the phone, centred, framed mid-shot on the phone screen. Action: she talks to the phone for 2 s, then reaches her right arm straight forward toward the phone so her hand (in real life) comes past the phone's edge, into Camera A's view in front of the screen, and her index finger taps the red Record button on the phone screen. Hold the tap 0.5 s, pull the hand back, keep talking. Line before the reach: 'Let me start this for you.' Takes: 5. Do one with her arm coming from directly behind the phone so the hand appears to emerge from the screen. Avoid sleeves covering the hand, the arm entering from the side of the frame, and shaking the phone on the tap (use a heavy tripod).

89 zoom-wheel: Same phone-on-tripod set (Canon behind the phone, phone filling ~70% of frame height, warm room). The phone runs its real camera app with Hiral on screen. Shoot 1 (the real thing): Hiral sits ~1.5 m from the phone; an off-screen helper's (or Hiral's own) hand comes in from the bottom of Camera A's frame, long-presses the '1x' button so the iPhone zoom wheel fans out, and slowly drags it from 0.5x to ~5x over 2 s while Hiral leans in slightly and widens her eyes. Hold 1 s at the close-up. Line at the close-up: 'Now that's a close-up on your money.' Takes: 5, varying drag speed. Shoot 2: the same with the hand only (Hiral seated, no dialogue) as a spare. Avoid a dim phone screen (max brightness), reflections, and the hand covering the dial numbers.

Seated at a clear desk

35 keycap-rain-land

35 keycap-rain-land: Camera: phone on a tripod, vertical 9:16, 1x lens (no zoom), lens at Hiral's chest height, about 1.5 m away. Framing: Hiral seated at a desk, from the top of her head (leave a hand's width of space above it) down to the desk; at least the front 25-30 cm of a CLEAR, empty desk surface visible across the bottom fifth of the frame (move papers, laptop and books off). Background: plain wall or tidy shelf, soft light from a window to one side, no direct sun. Wardrobe: solid colour top (no stripes). Action: 1) Look at camera and say the line for about 4 seconds (e.g. 'SIP, budget, Nifty... all these words keep landing on you.'). 2) On 'landing', look down at the desk for one beat, then back up. 3) Keep hands in her lap or at the sides of the desk, not in the centre, so the keys have room to land. Record 3 takes, plus 5 seconds of the empty desk and chair with no one in it (do not move the camera). Avoid: camera moving between takes, objects on the desk, leaning on the desk.

Tap the air on 'follow'

47 tap

47 tap: Camera: phone, vertical 9:16, on tripod at her eye height, 1 m away, 1x lens. Frame: head to waist, centred, plain wall or sofa behind, soft window light from the front. Hiral talks to camera for 2 s, then on the word 'follow' raises her right index finger and taps the air firmly once at shoulder height, about 25 cm to the right of her body (her right), holds the finger there for 0.5 s, smiles, drops the hand and keeps talking for 2 s. Line: 'If this helped... hit follow.' with the tap on 'follow'. Get 5 takes; keep the tap point in the same spot each take. Avoid: tapping in front of her face, fast blurred gestures, a dark top that hides the hand.

Face camera, small side moves

56 locked-on

56 locked-on: Camera: phone, vertical, tripod at her eye height, 1.2 m away, 1x lens. Frame: head to waist, centred, plain or softly lit background. Hiral faces the lens the whole time. She talks naturally for 5 s and makes two small moves: at 1 s she leans 15 cm to her left, at 3 s she drifts 15 cm back to the right, so the camera has something to follow. Line: 'Hi, I'm Hiral, and I teach money like a game.' Get 4 takes. Avoid: turning to profile, walking out of frame, hair across the face.

A room with real depth

84 vertigo

84 vertigo: Camera: Canon (or phone), vertical, on a tripod at Hiral's eye height, ~1.5-2 m away, 35 mm-equivalent. Location: a room with real DEPTH behind her, at least 4 m of visible space (a corridor, a classroom with rows of chairs, or a living room with a bookshelf and window at the far end). Not the patterned wallpaper. Even light on her face, background a little darker. Shoot 1: Hiral stands still, talking to camera, for 8 s; say the line in the edit ('That's when the whole picture changes') once in the middle. Shoot 2: empty room plate, same camera and framing, 5 s with Hiral out of shot. Best version: a real dolly. Put the tripod on a rolling chair/trolley and pull back 1.5 m while zooming in (or walk the phone back) so her face stays the same size; 3 takes. Avoid moving her head a lot, a flat wall behind her, and backlight from a window behind her.

What we learned

  1. No faces in the background. The effects lock onto the biggest face they find. On the Clear Tax shot a painted face on the wall took over and pushed the comment sheet off screen. Posters, paintings and TVs showing people all count.
  2. Shoot 2 seconds of the empty frame. Dolly-zoom, head-stack and blow-away show what is behind her. Without a real empty plate that area is guessed, and it smears (36 to 60% of it on our phone takes). Only the Canon tripod shoot had one.
  3. Keep the first second still. Three takes started with a handheld jump or a pan from the table. Every effect starts at 0.4 s, so a wobble there ruins it. Start talking, then hold the camera still.
  4. Headroom decides what fits above the head. Comment sheets, toggles, search bars and headlines need a quarter of the frame free above her hair. A tight chest-up shot pushes them onto her head.
  5. Thin lines need a plain wall. Pencil words, the text ring and backdrop words disappear into the jungle wallpaper. On the plain white wall they read at full contrast.
  6. Logos orbit, pictures carousel. Orbit tiles are small and moving: use bold single logos. Carousel cards are big and slow down: use reel covers and posts with text. Carousel spin at turns 0.55.
  7. Off-centre helps the tunnel, but not enough. Rabbit hole improved on the off-centre boardroom shot and still crosses her face twice. It needs her on a third line of the frame. It is the one effect still at 8.5.
  8. Phone takes are HDR. iPhone footage is 4K HLG. Convert it with avconvert first or skin goes grey and flat. 4K also keeps punch-ins and slow pushes sharp.

All effects

01backdrop-word

8.8
Audit 24 Nov: not verified — needs Vibha's reel (motion, or the grid label is shifted)

Reel 0:00

DH1 · plain wall, standing

A giant word behind the head needs a flat wall: on plain white it reads at full contrast and the cut-out edge is clean.

v06Match 8.8Looks 8.6Technical 8.9Overall 8.8

Same treatment: a giant edge-cropped condensed serif drops in with motion blur behind a clean hair matte, and the colour is now warm coral. What still separates it from the original is the missing soft glow and luminance lift, so the word looks printed on the wall rather than lit.

  • Glow: the original's letters bloom softly into the lamp-lit background, so the word reads as light in the room; ours are crisp, flat fills with no halo, which side by side looks more like print on the wall
  • Luminance: the original word is brighter than its surroundings (it glows over a mid-tone room). Ours sits on a near-white wall at similar brightness and only reads by hue, so it carries less punch at thumbnail size
  • Colour is now close: warm coral against the original's salmon-pink. Ours is still a touch more pink/magenta, which is minor
How to close the gap (3)
  1. Add a soft outer bloom: the text layer blurred at a radius of about 1.5-2% of frame width, screened at 30-40% opacity under the crisp letters
  2. Darken or warm the plate slightly behind the word band (a gentle vignette or a -5 to -8% exposure dip) so the word sits brighter than the wall, as in the original
  3. Optional: nudge the hue 5-8 degrees toward orange (about #F2A08E)

02sketch-words

7.3

Reel 0:05

DH1 · plain wall, standing

Pencil strokes are thin; a plain wall is the only background they read on.

Changed in testing: Raised to y=330: at 610 the line crossed her head.

v03Match 7.4Looks 7.2Technical 7.6Overall 7.3

Clean, bug-free version of the right effect (hatched maroon serif, pencil lead word, ruled paper, gold underline, hard cut, i-dot and descender fixed), but the word is too small and lands too late to hit like the original.

  • Scale: the big word is only ~170px tall in a 1920px frame (~9% of height) and spans ~80% width; in the original the hatched word is the dominant element (~20% of frame height, letters chunky and heavy), so ours reads as a header strip rather than a takeover
  • Timing: the paper cuts in at 2.0s but the lead word writes slowly until ~3.8s and 'receipts' only finishes around 4.5s, leaving under 1s of full hold before the 5.5s end; the original lands the big word fast and holds it
  • Lead word 'electronic gold' is still a clean, even monoline marker face; the original 'sketch' is a scratchy, uneven graphite pencil hand
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Scale the big word up ~1.6x (cap height ~280px), allow it to run near full width with tighter tracking, and lower the block so the underline sits ~20px above the hairline
  2. Retime: lead word written in ~0.5s starting at the paper cut (2.0s), big word outline 2.5-3.3s, hatch fill 3.3-3.7s, underline 3.7-3.9s, then hold ~1.5s
  3. Swap the lead word to a rough pencil script (e.g. Reenie Beanie or Caveat with 1-2px jitter, graphite #3a3a3a at ~85% opacity, slight grain)
  4. Randomise hatch angle +/-6 deg, spacing and stroke weight per line, add a second offset pencil pass to the outline and a light grain multiply over the fill
  5. Warm the paper toward #F2EBDD and add a faint fibre texture plus soft vignette

03day-dial

7.3

Reel 0:11

DH2 · plain wall, standing

The text ring passes behind the head; a flat wall keeps every word of the ring legible.

Changed in testing: Solid 3D letters: 16-layer extrusion, light bevel, contact shadow, 18° perspective tilt, slower spin (60°/s).

v02Match 7.5Looks 7.5Technical 7Overall 7.3

The right effect, well drawn: paper clock dial, serif numerals, italic labels and a black wedge wipe. But the wedge stops sweeping during the hold, and a stray gold line through the 12 and a doubled 11 cost it the 9.

  • The hold is static. In the original the black wedge keeps sweeping round the dial for the whole beat. In ours the wedge wipes in, then the dial sits still for about 2.5 s with no wedge, and the wedge only comes back on the exit. The motion that defines the effect is missing for most of the clip.
  • A stray thin gold vertical line runs from the top of the frame to the dial centre. It cuts through the '12' and the 'Dhanteras' label and reads as a render artefact, not a clock hand. The original has nothing like it.
  • The '11' looks doubled ('1\1') because a segment divider or tick runs through the numeral. The original keeps its numerals clean.
How to close the gap (6)
  1. Keep the wedge rotating through the hold, at roughly 90-120 deg/s clockwise, with the light-ray glint on its leading edge. Never let it disappear between the entry and exit wipes.
  2. Remove the gold vertical line, or make it a real tapered clock hand that starts at the dial centre and stays inside the dial.
  3. Clip the segment divider and tick lines so they stop short of the numeral glyphs, with a knock-out mask around each numeral.
  4. Warm the paper plate (about +4 to +6 in R/Y, a slight vignette) and add the soft shadow or fold edge the original has on the panel.
  5. Choke the matte by 1-2 px and despill the light fringe on the body edge before the drop shadow is applied.
  6. Optional: put one highlighted word in reverse white inside the wedge as it passes each segment, matching the original's active-label read.

04dot-reveal

8.4
Art-director audit 24 Nov: 8 vs Vibha's frame

Reel 0:16

DH2 · plain wall, standing

The dot pattern needs a strong figure/ground split: magenta dress on white.

v04Match 8.5Looks 8.2Technical 8.5Overall 8.4

Gold clumped mosaic now matches cell 34 closely and Hiral's face reads; the wall is still too bright and the snap fades rather than resolves.

  • Background wall is still brighter and busier than the original (cell 34): ours is an even field of lit gold and cream dots edge to edge, while the original dims toward the bottom and keeps the figure as the clear focal shape
  • The snap is now a short crossfade (~4.0-4.2 s) with dots still visible over the picture, which is better than v03's hard cut, but the dots fade rather than shrink or resolve into the image, so the reveal reads as a dissolve
  • The face now holds mid-tone dots and is recognisable, but the lower body is still a dark maroon block with little dot texture, so the figure reads as a head on a dark shape
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Dim background dots ~20% and add a soft bottom vignette falling to ~60% brightness at the hem, as in the original
  2. Over the 4-6 transition frames, shrink the cell pitch to about 1/3 while crossfading, so the mosaic sharpens into the picture instead of fading off it
  3. Lift subject luminance below the chest (gamma ~0.85 inside the matte, below shoulder line) so the dress shows dot texture
  4. Trim the plain tail to ~0.8 s or hold the mosaic 0.4 s longer

Clones overlap each other; a plain wall hides any matte seam between copies.

v03Match 8Looks 7.5Technical 7.8Overall 7.8

Now clearly the same effect: chest-up punch-in, dimmed clones fanning out behind Hiral on cue for about 1 s. What still separates it from the original is the grey-patch grade on a bright wall and clones that stay too pink to recede.

  • Grade/room: the original's clones melt into a dark, moody room so the stack reads as depth for free. On our light wall the fix is a grey vignette that darkens the plate only around the clones, so the frame visibly turns muddy-grey for ~1 s and then lightens again. It reads as an applied shadow, not as a room
  • The clones are still too saturated. Slots 1-2 stay strong magenta, and against the greyed wall they pop forward instead of receding. In the reference the rear heads go almost to silhouette
  • The lower-body fade is better (grey, no white haze), but the clones still end in a visible soft horizontal fade at chest height on both sides. The reference clones run behind the master's shoulders into darkness with no visible end line
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Stretch the plate darkening into a full-frame grade (about -18% exposure, -20% saturation on the background matte only) with 6-frame ramps, instead of a local vignette around the clone zone, so the room goes dark rather than getting a grey patch
  2. Push the clone grade further: brightness about 0.70/0.58/0.48/0.40 and saturation about 0.55/0.45/0.38/0.32, plus a slight cool shift on slots 3-4
  3. Start the clone alpha fade lower and let it pass behind the master's shoulders (fade over 2.2x face width, starting 1.0x below the chin), so no fade line is visible beside her
  4. Drop to 3 clones per side and cut the slot-1 offset about 10% so each clone tucks under the one in front by about 40% of a head
  5. Fade the clone alpha to 0 within the first 2 frames of the whip-out so the blur has no hard doubled edge, and keep the caption pills on screen through the end of the clip

19code-body

7.5

Reel 1:39

DH5 · plain wall, standing

Code fills the whole silhouette, so the body needs a clean edge: on a plain white wall the matte is crisp and the solid code body reads at a glance. On the Clear Tax shot the painted faces behind her and a soft matte on the trousers made it look broken.

Changed in testing: Rebuilt: solid code body (dim glyph grid + two bright streams per column), glowing rim, scan-line wipe in and out; moved to the plain white wall, so the matte is clean.

v02Match 7.5Looks 7.5Technical 8Overall 7.5

Right effect, right grade and a recognisable Hiral made of code in a dark room; it just resolves to text too fine to read and the background code is too thin.

  • Settled state resolves too fine: cells end at ~9x15 px on a 1080-wide frame, so the body reads as a halftone texture and the code inside her is illegible at phone size; the original holds ~20 px cells where the person is a chunky mosaic AND the lines of code are readable word by word
  • Background code is too small and too sparse once settled (tiny single-size lines with big empty gaps); the original fills the room with denser, mixed-size, slightly soft code at varied brightness, giving depth
  • Original has bright near-white highlight cells (face, hands) punching out of the mosaic; ours is more even, the cream highlights are smaller and the face reads as a photo rather than as glyph blocks
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Stop the resolve at the second stage (cell ~15x21, font ~25 px) or hold around 17-20 px cells for the whole hold, so the code inside the body is readable on a phone
  2. Render background code at 2-3 sizes (18/24/30 px), 25-40% opacity with a 1-2 px blur on the larger rows, and fill 70-80% of rows instead of scattered lines
  3. Push the top of the palette: map the brightest 10% of luminance to pure #FAF8F0 cells with dark text, so face and hands pop as in the reference
  4. Keep the top-down wipe-in and bottom-up wipe-out; they are clean

  • The clip is short: the card arrives around 1s, the third toggle lands at about 3.9s and the all-on state holds for only about 1.5s, with no settle or exit beat
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Raise the eased zoom to about 1.10-1.15 over the clip so the push reads
  2. Extend the clip, or bring the card in at 0.5s, so the all-on state holds for 2s or more, then add a small settle (a 1.02 scale breath) at the end
  3. Feather the person matte 1-2px at the crown, and keep the 2px choke, so the hair edge softens against the white card
  4. Add a 1.05 scale overshoot to each switch as it flips, and give the card a slightly stronger soft shadow or a frosted fill so it lifts off the wood

No visual reference in the original; judged on the written description.

CT2 · wide with headroom

Video tiles circle the torso and pass behind her, so the whole torso must be in frame with room on both sides for the ring.

Changed in testing: Rebuilt: six real IFM game-promo reels orbit as 9:16 video tiles, far side behind her and near side in front, depth-scaled; room dimmed 40% so the videos carry the frame.

v03Match 7.5Looks 7.5Technical 8Overall 7.5

Big step up from v02: the close framing and the heavier gold serif read well, and the front/back occlusion is clean. The ring is still too narrow and tight to the face (side letters stack vertically, nothing passes over the head), so it hugs the face where the reel's ring is a wide halo.

  • Ring geometry: ours is a tall, narrow ellipse. The side letters stack into near-vertical columns beside the cheeks (F/U/N, U/F) and the back arc never shows above the head. The reel's ring is a wide, gently tilted ellipse: its back letters ride up and over the cap (G N I at the top) and its sides fan out past the shoulders
  • The ring sits high and tight. The front arc crosses at chin and jaw level and the ring is only slightly wider than the face. The reel's ring spans about 1.5x head width with the front word on the beard/neckline, so it reads as a halo around the head, not text hugging the face
  • Grade is barely touched. The reel is low-key and moody, so the gold front glyphs pop. Ours sits on a flat grey-green wall with bright skin, so the gold reads lower contrast
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Widen the ellipse: radius X about 0.75x head height each side of the face centre, radius Y about 0.18x of X, tilted 8-10 degrees. Lift the back arc so it passes behind the crown/hair top and shows letters above the head
  2. Lower the ring centre by about 6-8% of frame height so the front arc lands on the jaw/neck line and the back arc on the hairline-to-crown
  3. Deepen the grade 12-15% (lift blacks less, pull mids) during the effect window, and add a soft warm glow and drop shadow under the front glyphs
  4. Make the whip-in readable: 5-6 frames of letters spiralling in from a larger radius, with motion blur and an opacity ramp, mirrored on the exit
  5. Lay the front glyphs out by advance width along the arc, and narrow the separator dot's slot so 'MUTUAL FUND' reads as set type

How to close the gap (5)

  3. Swap chip labels on a hard cut (or a <=2-frame fade) per keystroke; draw the accept ring outside the label and remove the ring once the gold fill lands
  4. Find and remove the dark element behind the chip row (likely the tap-ring or pop-up layer drawn at rest); render it only during a tap
  5. Bring the keyboard in by ~0.5s with a short slide-up, and make the key pop-up ~1.2x taller with a solid fill and soft shadow like the original

Same effect, recognisably: red double-border NOPE slams in with a 1-frame overshoot and holds about 2 s, but it is smaller, sits higher, and is heavier and cleaner than Vibha's ink stamp, and it drifts slightly after landing.

  • Scale and placement: Vibha's NOPE stamp is larger, spans the full frame width and runs off the right edge, sitting low over the waist and lap. Ours is about 75% of the frame width and sits higher, mid-torso, so it reads as a sticker more than a stamp hitting the frame.

  • Blend: the reference reads as multiply ink that shows the fabric and skin through it. Ours is more opaque and tints the hands pink in front of the body, and the hands sit in front of the stamp in some frames and behind it in others (for example 2.4 s vs 4.4 s).
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Scale the stamp up about 1.3x and move its centre down to the waist line (about y=0.66 of the frame), letting the right end bleed off-frame at about -18 degrees, as in the reference.
  2. Use a lighter slab or stencil serif (or reduce the stroke weight) and apply a stronger distress mask (speckle plus edge erosion) to both the letters and the double border.
  3. Composite with multiply at about 85% opacity instead of normal alpha, and pick one hand-occlusion rule (stamp always over the hands) for the whole hold.
  4. Lock the stamp's position from the frame after impact. Keep the 1-frame oversized ghost and settle, but remove the residual drift.

  • No visual reference for the 'land' variant; judged against shortcut-rain cell 17 and the skill text. Keycaps themselves match cell 17 closely (big white 3D caps, single glyphs, slight tilt)
  • The pile is a neat 4-3-1 pyramid hovering over her lap with no contact shadow or squash; it reads as stacked stickers, not keys that landed on something
  • Pile sits in front of her right hand and wrist and covers them for ~2 s; cell 17's keys stay in the upper frame around/behind the head and never cover the body
What Hiral needs to do

Camera: phone on a tripod, vertical 9:16, 1x lens (no zoom), lens at Hiral's chest height, about 1.5 m away. Framing: Hiral seated at a desk, from the top of her head (leave a hand's width of space above it) down to the desk; at least the front 25-30 cm of a CLEAR, empty desk surface visible across the bottom fifth of the frame (move papers, laptop and books off). Background: plain wall or tidy shelf, soft light from a window to one side, no direct sun. Wardrobe: solid colour top (no stripes). Action: 1) Look at camera and say the line for about 4 seconds (e.g. 'SIP, budget, Nifty... all these words keep landing on you.'). 2) On 'landing', look down at the desk for one beat, then back up. 3) Keep hands in her lap or at the sides of the desk, not in the centre, so the keys have room to land. Record 3 takes, plus 5 seconds of the empty desk and chair with no one in it (do not move the camera). Avoid: camera moving between takes, objects on the desk, leaning on the desk.

Software changes after the shoot (3)
  1. Once footage exists: make keys fall from above frame and land with bounce on the real desk surface (floor = desk line), piling with slight rotation
  2. Use big 3D keycaps with single glyphs as in #29
  3. Keep the pile visible to the end, or knock it away on a beat instead of greying it out

No visual reference in the original; judged on the written description.

7.5

Reel 3:38

RS1 · seated off-centre, deep room

Focus pulls to the background; a deep boardroom gives the background something to resolve into.

v02Match 7.5Looks 7.5Technical 7.5Overall 7.5

Fixed the v01 reversal: Hiral stays sharp while the room melts. It reads as the right effect, but it un-racks too soon and lacks the reference's bokeh glow.

  • Blur ramps back out to fully sharp at about 2.8 s. The original pulls focus once to the speaker and holds the soft background until the next cut, so ours reads as a focus wobble rather than a decisive rack
  • The plate is bright, flat office light with no point sources. The original's dark room turns the lamps and frame into soft bokeh blobs, and that bokeh is what sells the lens. Ours looks more like a phone portrait-mode blur

How to close the gap (5)
  1. Ramp in over 0.4 s (ease-out), then hold the blur to the end of the segment or the next cut instead of ramping back. If a return is needed, make it a separate, faster 0.25 s snap
  2. Use a disc/hexagonal lens kernel and lift highlights before blurring (or a slight background grade-down of ~10%) so the shelf items and window light bloom into bokeh as in the reference
  3. Either crop/position so the book sits lower or out of frame, or give the foreground a lighter blur radius than the back wall (depth-weighted) so the IFM cover stays recognisable
  4. Erode the subject matte 4-6 px along the forearm/desk contact line and feather it so no sharp desk sliver survives
  5. Raise the far-plane blur radius ~25% to match the original's separation

  2. Widen the rotation to about -22/-8/+8/+22 deg and increase the x-spacing about 15% so each headline clears the next phone. Check that 'Gold better than Stocks' is fully readable

51banknote

7.5

Reel 4:33

DN3 · close-up

The engraved portrait sits in a small oval; a close-up face fills it.

v02Match 8Looks 7.5Technical 7Overall 7.5

Now clearly the same effect: an upright, full-bleed green engraved note with a guilloche oval, microtext ring, rosettes, serial, corner values and a counting serif denomination, hard cut in and out. Held back by a muddy, unflattering engraved face, an overflowing footer pill and a sparser tall layout.

  • Engraved portrait is harsher and muddier than the original: the line screen crushes Hiral's mid-tones, so the face reads aged and the mouth smears into a dark blot on several frames, where the original's engraving keeps clean, flattering facial planes with crisp highlights
  • Footer pill text overflows its frame: 'THIS NOTE IS NOT MONEY. / THE FOLLOWERS ARE REAL.' runs over the left and right double-rule borders of its box
  • 9:16 adaptation stretches the oval portrait tall and leaves wide empty paper between the oval and the side borders; the original's square note is denser, with the portrait, rosettes and denomination box packed tightly
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Engraving pass: lift the face's mid-tones before line-screening (gamma about 0.8 on the face matte, plus a local-contrast or clarity boost), cap the maximum line thickness on skin, and keep the lips and teeth as clean highlights so the mouth never fills in
  2. Shrink the footer copy to fit inside the inner rule with at least 14 px of padding, or widen the centre pill; check every text box for overflow with a bbox test
  3. Use the extra vertical space: either widen the oval to the original's proportions and add a guilloche band or microtext panel above and below, or move the denomination box up so the paper is evenly dense
  4. Use a larger, real IFM number for the denomination (for example total students or followers with Indian grouping, '1,24,635.') so the count-up ticks through more digits and fills the box as the original does
  5. Raise the face about 40 px in the oval and pull both rosettes fully clear of the oval ring

54live-cursor

6

Reel 4:50

CL1 · classroom

A bounding box around the teacher in a busy room says 'this one'.

v02Match 7Looks 6.5Technical 5Overall 6

This is now clearly the same effect, with a tracked gold box, 8 handles, a WxH tag and a Hiral pill. A bright cutout halo, box jitter and no actual drag keep it well short of the original.

  • A pale halo with stair-stepped edges outlines her hair, shoulders and arms in every frame, even after the box has gone. The cutout is composited over a darker plate. The reference has no cutout seam at all.
  • The box size jumps between frames (560x889, 527x837, 541x859, 566x898, 544x864) and reads as jitter. In the reference the box holds steady or changes because the cursor is dragging it.
  • The cursor sits parked on the bottom-right handle with a ring. It never visibly drags or resizes the box, so the 'live' part is weak.
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Remove the halo. Composite the overlay straight onto the original frame with no cutout and no plate regrade, or choke the matte 2-3px and feather it 1-2px, and match the plate grade to the source.
  2. Smooth the face-driven box with an EMA or one-euro filter (around 0.15) so it stays steady. Change its size only during a scripted drag and let the dimension tag count up during that drag.
  3. Animate one real drag: the cursor grabs the bottom-right handle and pulls it out by about 60-80px over 0.4s, the box follows, the tag updates, and then it releases.
  4. Extend the box bottom to about the waist or hand line, so it reads as a head-to-hands selection like the reference.
  5. Thin the stroke to 2px gold and shrink the handles to about 14px white squares.

CL2 · classroom

A newspaper front page with a class photo is a real IFM story (the class is the news).

v02Match 8Looks 8Technical 7.7Overall 7.9

Now unmistakably the same broadsheet effect with live halftone Hiral and smart IFM copy; a lighter headline, coarse halftone and hard-cut exit keep it just short of a twin.

  • Headline weight: the ref's '20 VIDEO EFFECTS' is a heavy, tightly condensed display serif filling the measure; ours ('635 FOLLOWERS') is a lighter, wider book serif, so the page reads quieter and less tabloid-punchy
  • Halftone is coarser and harsher than the ref: big dots with blown highlights on the face, where the ref keeps a finer screen with mid-greys and a softer tonal face
  • Exit is a hard cut back to the talking head; the ref leaves the page via a torn-paper reveal of the live speaker (the next beat), so the end of ours lacks the ref's payoff
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Swap the headline to a bold condensed serif (e.g. a Bodoni/Playfair Display Condensed or Oswald-like serif condensed at 700) and size it to fill the column width
  2. Halftone: reduce dot cell by ~30%, lift gamma on the face before screening and clamp highlights so cheeks keep grey dots instead of blank paper
  3. End on a torn-paper split (two halves pulling apart) revealing the live clip underneath, as the ref does, instead of a hard cut
  4. Turn off full justification in the narrow side columns (ragged-right or hyphenate) to remove the rivers
  5. Widen the photo window toward 4:5 and crop to head and shoulders so the face occupies a larger share of the page

64impact-frame

6.5

Reel 5:44

Canon 0276 · tripod + empty plate

Threshold flash needs strong lighting contrast; the studio key light gives a crisp B&W.

v02Match 7Looks 6.5Technical 6Overall 6.5

Now clearly the same comic impact panel (cream speed-burst, black silhouette, huge bold word across the chest), but the threshold face and the noisy hand stop it from matching the reference's clean ink portrait.

  • Face is a raw 2-tone threshold, not ink line-art: eye sockets fill solid black on the first frames, the mouth and teeth turn into blotches, and the cheeks are pocked with specks. The reference has clean contour lines and a readable, flattering face
  • The hand by her chin (frames 3-4) and the right forearm at the lower edge break up into checkered threshold noise; the reference has no such debris
  • It holds about 1.0 s (2.50-3.47 s), longer than the reference's ~0.6 s and the catalogue's 0.3-0.8 s, so the cut hits less hard
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Build the face from edge lines (Canny/XDoG on a bilateral-smoothed luma, then dilate 1-2 px) over a cream fill, and keep the threshold only for hair and clothing; lift the face exposure before thresholding so the eyes and teeth stay open
  2. Remove small connected components (<~400 px) and fill holes in the subject mask; crop or matte out the lower-right arm and soften the hand region with the same line-art pass
  3. Trim the hold to 0.5-0.6 s (15-18 frames) and use 2-3 held drawings on twos instead of re-thresholding every frame
  4. Add a thin cream inner contour along the hair/dress boundary and the neckline so the silhouette has the drawn edge the reference has

Now clearly the same effect (dark green, white wire planes, serif title, list, red waveform), but clipped framing, a half-filled room plane and an overlong static hold keep it short of the ref.

  6. Draw floor/edge lines for planes in front of ME after the cutout only where they are truly in front; mask lines behind her by the cutout alpha; enlarge the waveform along the front base

66blow-away

7

Reel 5:55

Canon 0281 · tripod + empty plate

She dissolves and leaves the empty set: only the Canon shoot has a TRUE empty plate.

v02Match 7.2Looks 7Technical 6.8Overall 7

Much closer than v01: fine, subject-coloured dust and a clean empty plate. But the half-eaten body goes ghostly-transparent, and the dust falls like sand instead of blowing away up and to the side.

  • Mid-dissolve the unconsumed body turns semi-transparent: at ~3.5-3.7s the face and hair are a see-through ghost with the frog mural showing through, so it reads as an opacity fade plus grain. In the ref the part not yet eaten stays fully solid and crisp right up to the erosion front

  • Erosion order is a broad left-to-right wipe across head and torso at once. The ref starts at the gesturing hand, travels up the arm and body and takes the cap/head last as a distinct beat
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Keep alpha at 1.0 for every pixel behind the erosion front. Only pixels that the noise mask has converted to particles may leave; no global or regional opacity ramp on the remaining cutout
  2. Give particles a horizontal wind vector (to frame-left) with upward lift of about -0.3 to -0.5 of horizontal speed, plus curl-noise turbulence; drop gravity to near zero and fade each particle over 0.5-0.7 s so nothing piles up at the bottom
  3. Seed the dissolve mask at her hand/forearm and propagate along the body with a noise-modulated front, reaching the head last (about 0.3 s after the torso)
  4. Thin the emission: about 40-60% fewer particles, 1-3 px, with brightness jitter so dark-dress specks still read against the grey mural
  5. Kill or fade all particles before they reach the frame edge, and hold the clean plate for at least 0.8 s, as now

  • Headline is set in a tall compressed condensed face ('MONEY CLASS, 11 TO 2') that looks horizontally squeezed; ref uses a wide high-contrast Didone with more weight and breathing room
  • A thin white pre-crack line creeps down the page for ~0.3 s before the rip; ref holds a clean page and rips in one beat, so ours has a slightly slower, telegraphed start
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Animate each half with outward translation plus 1.10-1.25x scale toward camera, 8-12 deg rotation and a slight perspective skew/curl so they fly past the lens off-frame in 0.25-0.35 s
  2. Swap the headline to a wide bold Didone (e.g. Playfair Display Black / Bodoni Moda Bold) at the ref's proportions, two lines if needed, instead of the condensed face
  3. Cut the pre-crack to <=3 frames or drop it; hold the clean page, then rip on the whoosh transient
  4. Darken/desaturate the revealed plate slightly for the first 10 frames (or add a brief vignette) so the cream halves separate strongly from the background
  5. Add a soft drop shadow under each half onto the revealed video to sell depth

68dolly-zoom

7.7

Reel 6:06

Canon 0283 · tripod + empty plate

Vertigo scales the background behind her, so it needs a TRUE empty-set plate. On the boardroom take the guessed background smeared into dark blobs; only the Canon shoot has a real plate.

Changed in testing: Moved from the boardroom (guessed plate smeared) to Canon MVI_0283 with the true plate.

v02Match 7.6Looks 7.4Technical 8.3Overall 7.7

A clean, convincing cutout over a smooth 1.5x push that holds; the flat, landmark-free mural and bright grade make it read as a background zoom more than the original's moody room-swell.

  • Ours zooms a flat, evenly busy wall mural with no depth landmarks. The original works because a real room swells behind him: the picture frame grows and the lamp leaves the frame. On ours it reads more as 'the wallpaper zoomed' than as a lens or vertigo move
  • The grade is bright, flat grey daylight. The original is dark and warm with a vignette that pulls the eye to the face, so ours has less of the tension a dolly zoom is meant to create
  • The push is about 1.5x over 1.3 s and is smooth. It is about as strong as the original but a little slower; the original lands in about 1 s
How to close the gap (4)
  1. Shoot or pick a plate with depth cues at different distances (a frame, shelf, lamp or doorway edge, the counter line) so the background scale change is obvious. Or composite a single framed IFM poster onto the mural near her head as a size reference
  2. Darken and warm the plate only, down about 0.6 EV with a soft vignette, keeping Hiral at her current exposure so she separates the way the original subject does
  3. Shorten the push to about 1.0 s (T0 to T1) and keep the hold
  4. Halve the plate motion-blur samples so the mural stays readable mid-move

69head-stack

7.4

Reel 6:12

Canon 0283 · tripod + empty plate

Stacked heads leave the background exposed below them; on a close-up 60% of that background is guessed and turns to mush. Needs a real plate: Canon shoot.

Changed in testing: Moved from the close-up (60% guessed plate) to Canon MVI_0283.

v02Match 7.6Looks 7.2Technical 7.5Overall 7.4

Now the right effect: cream mono tags drop, stack on her head and a side stack, then get swatted off with blur; it loses points on a floating base tag, an unsupported side stack and the busy painting behind.

  • The bottom head tag hovers about 20-30px above her hair (clear gap at ~3.3s); in the original the lowest tag sits pressed onto the cap, so the stack reads as resting on him, not floating
  • The second stack (Debt / Nifty / Rainy day) hangs in mid-air beside her head at hair level; in the original it sits on his raised palm / shoulder, so it is physically held. Here her hands are clasped at waist height while it floats
  • Busy, high-contrast charcoal painting directly behind the head stack competes with the white tags; the original has a near-black wall so the cream tags pop. No shadow or local darkening compensates
How to close the gap (5)
  1. Lower the head-stack anchor so the bottom tag overlaps the hair crown by ~6-10px (or occlude it slightly with the matte) and add a 1-2 frame squash on each landing
  2. Anchor the side stack to a tracked open palm or the shoulder line in frames where it is held; if no raised hand exists in the clip, move it to rest on her shoulder (matte top at screen-left) rather than mid-air
  3. Add a soft 35-50% dark drop shadow under each tag and a gentle vignette/darken of the painting region behind the stack so the tags separate from the artwork
  4. Increase per-tag x-jitter to ±25px and rotation to ±6-8 degrees, alternating, so the pile looks precarious like the original
  5. Scale tags up ~10-15% (TH 62 to ~70) so the stack width approaches her head width

      New · 14 Nov · phone-canvas-edit-fx

      Canon 0283 · tripod + empty plate

      The room stretches behind her while she stays the same size. Only works with a real empty-set plate (Canon MVI_0270 at 10.5 s here).

      Changed from the stock skill: Stock shrank her and showed black bars and a ghost of her body; now true plate, subject locked.

      v01Match 3Looks 4.5Technical 5.5Overall 3

      Needs new Hiral video

      On a flat wall the dolly zoom has nothing to stretch; it's effectively invisible.

      • A flat wallpaper wall has no depth, so scaling it 1.0 → 1.55 reads as the wallpaper getting bigger, not as a dolly zoom. The original has a deep room (bookshelf, window, plants) that stretches
      • Most viewers won't notice anything happened in our version
      • The original stacks a bold two-tone caption ('NEW FRAME' / 'NEW MOOD')
      What Hiral needs to do

      Camera: Canon (or phone), vertical, on a tripod at Hiral's eye height, ~1.5-2 m away, 35 mm-equivalent. Location: a room with real DEPTH behind her, at least 4 m of visible space (a corridor, a classroom with rows of chairs, or a living room with a bookshelf and window at the far end). Not the patterned wallpaper. Even light on her face, background a little darker. Shoot 1: Hiral stands still, talking to camera, for 8 s; say the line in the edit ('That's when the whole picture changes') once in the middle. Shoot 2: empty room plate, same camera and framing, 5 s with Hiral out of shot. Best version: a real dolly. Put the tripod on a rolling chair/trolley and pull back 1.5 m while zooming in (or walk the phone back) so her face stays the same size; 3 takes. Avoid moving her head a lot, a flat wall behind her, and backlight from a window behind her.

      Software changes after the shoot (3)
      1. After the new footage: run the bg/subject opposite-scale on the deep-room plate, keeping her face size locked

      3. Interim software-only option: replace the plate with a deep-room photo (a workshop room) to get some perspective cue

      v01Match 1.5Looks 3Technical 3Overall 2

      Needs new Hiral video

      Nowhere close, as the client said: no phone, no room and she never moves, so there is no slam to show.

      • The original is a REAL phone on a tripod in a room, filmed from behind; she walks from the back of the room up to the phone and presses her face and both palms flat against the glass (squashed nose, cheeks). Ours is a full-screen camera UI with no phone, room or tripod
      • Hiral never moves toward camera; she stands and talks, so there is no slam
      • Semi-transparent grey composited hands ghost over her body at ~1.5 s: an obvious artefact
      What Hiral needs to do

      Two cameras. Camera A (Canon, the hero shot): vertical, on a tripod, ~60 cm behind a phone that is itself on a small tripod; frame so the phone fills ~70% of the height with the room visible around it, focus on the phone screen. The phone (camera B): iPhone in video mode, rear camera facing Hiral, screen facing camera A, brightness at max, Do Not Disturb on. Set: a homely room (bed, sofa or plants), warm light, phone ~1.2 m off the floor. Action: Hiral starts 3-4 m back from the phone, centred. On 'action' she walks briskly toward it (2 s), then leans in and presses both open palms and her face (cheek or nose) flat onto the phone screen, holds 1 s, smiles, pulls back. She can laugh. Total ~5 s. Line, optional, as she pulls back: 'Okay, now I have your attention.' Takes: 5, including one with only palms (no face) as a safe option. Clean the phone glass between takes. Avoid knocking the phone tripod (weigh it down), ceiling lights reflecting on the screen, and walking off-centre.
